stem:
Chetan expands $370$ by place value as $3\times100+7\times10+0\times1$. He asks why divisibility by $10$ depends only on the units digit being $0$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Every higher place is a multiple of $10$, so only the units digit can stop the whole number from being a multiple of $10$; here that digit is $0$.
The label that matters is the units digit alone, so place value plays no role in the shortcut.
The units digit is what creates place value, so start from that digit and ignore the expansion.
The answer is $0$ only because $0$ is the last digit printed in $370$.

teacher.key_rationale: Place-value expansion shows hundreds and tens are multiples of 10, so only the units digit can block divisibility by 10. Dropping place value for a bare units-digit label swaps the hinge. Reversing units digit as creating place value, or grabbing the printed 0, misses the mechanism.
